quests.instruction: What is the action word for eating with very small, gentle bites?
quests.question: Nibble
quests.hint: Think about how a hamster eats a tiny piece of carrot, bit by bit.
quests.explanation: Nibble means to eat with small, gentle bites. A hamster likes to nibble on seeds!
quests.funFact: Small animals like hamsters and rabbits often nibble their food slowly!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for chewing food loudly and happily?
quests.question: Munch
quests.hint: Think about crunching happily on a fresh, crispy carrot.
quests.explanation: Munch means to chew food loudly and happily. We munch on crunchy snacks like carrots!
quests.funFact: Crunchy foods like apples and carrots are extra fun to munch on!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for eating something very quickly, in big bites?
quests.question: Gobble
quests.hint: Think about eating super fast because you are extremely hungry.
quests.explanation: Gobble means to eat something very quickly in big bites. We gobble up food when we are very hungry!
quests.funFact: Turkeys make a funny sound called a gobble, which is where this word comes from too!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for swallowing a large amount of liquid quickly?
quests.question: Gulp
quests.hint: Think about drinking a whole glass of water in just a few big swallows.
quests.explanation: Gulp means to swallow a large amount quickly. We gulp down water after running outside!
quests.funFact: Gulping your drink too fast can sometimes give you the hiccups!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for drinking a small amount slowly?
quests.question: Sip
quests.hint: Think about taking one tiny, careful drink of hot soup.
quests.explanation: Sip means to drink a small amount slowly. We sip hot soup carefully so we do not burn our tongue!
quests.funFact: Sipping slowly is a great way to enjoy a drink that is very hot!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for drinking or eating noisily by sucking it in?
quests.question: Slurp
quests.hint: Think about the noisy sound of sucking up a long noodle.
quests.explanation: Slurp means to drink or eat noisily by sucking it in. We slurp long noodles from a bowl!
quests.funFact: In some countries, slurping your noodles loudly shows you are enjoying your meal!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for eating something completely and very eagerly?
quests.question: Devour
quests.hint: Think about finishing your whole favorite meal in no time because it tastes so good.
quests.explanation: Devour means to eat something completely and eagerly. We devour a delicious meal when we are starving!
quests.funFact: A hungry lion can devour a huge meal in a surprisingly short amount of time!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for eating a small amount of food between meals?
quests.question: Snack
quests.hint: Think about eating a few crackers in the afternoon before dinner.
quests.explanation: Snack means to eat a small amount of food between meals. We snack on fruit in the afternoon!
quests.funFact: A healthy snack can give you extra energy between breakfast and lunch!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for eating something slowly to enjoy every bit of the taste?
quests.question: Savor
quests.hint: Think about eating your favorite dessert slowly so you enjoy every single bite.
quests.explanation: Savor means to eat slowly and enjoy every bit of flavor. We savor a special treat on our birthday!
quests.funFact: Savoring your food slowly can help you notice flavors you might otherwise miss!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for taking a quick, secret look at something?
quests.question: Peek
quests.hint: Think about a quick little look through a slightly open door.
quests.explanation: Peek means to take a quick, secret look. We peek through a door to see a surprise!
quests.funFact: Peeking is a quick way to catch a glimpse without anyone noticing!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking at something for just a very short moment?
quests.question: Glance
quests.hint: Think about quickly checking a clock before looking back at your work.
quests.explanation: Glance means to look at something for a short moment. We glance at the clock to check the time!
quests.funFact: A quick glance can give you just enough information without stopping what you are doing!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking at something for a long time without looking away?
quests.question: Stare
quests.hint: Think about looking at a fascinating rainbow without looking away for a long while.
quests.explanation: Stare means to look at something for a long time. We stare at a beautiful rainbow in the sky!
quests.funFact: It is polite to stare at amazing things, like rainbows, rather than at people!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking softly and steadily at something you find wonderful?
quests.question: Gaze
quests.hint: Think about looking calmly up at the twinkling stars at night.
quests.explanation: Gaze means to look softly and steadily at something wonderful. We gaze up at the stars at night!
quests.funFact: People often gaze quietly at beautiful things like sunsets and starry skies!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for almost closing your eyes to see better in bright light?
quests.question: Squint
quests.hint: Think about scrunching your eyes almost shut when the sun is very bright.
quests.explanation: Squint means to almost close your eyes to see better. We squint when the sun is very bright!
quests.funFact: Squinting helps block out some bright light so your eyes can focus more clearly!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking very closely at something hard to see?
quests.question: Peer
quests.hint: Think about leaning in close to look carefully into a small, dark box.
quests.explanation: Peer means to look very closely at something hard to see. We peer into a dark box to find our toy!
quests.funFact: Peering closely at something can help you notice tiny details you missed before!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking at something very carefully to understand it?
quests.question: Examine
quests.hint: Think about looking very closely at a bug to see all of its tiny parts.
quests.explanation: Examine means to look at something very carefully. We examine a bug to learn how it moves!
quests.funFact: Doctors and scientists examine things closely to understand them fully!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for checking something carefully to make sure it is okay?
quests.question: Inspect
quests.hint: Think about checking a toy carefully to make sure nothing is broken.
quests.explanation: Inspect means to check something carefully. We inspect a toy to make sure it works well!
quests.funFact: Inspecting things carefully can help you catch small problems early!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for speaking quietly and unclearly, almost to yourself?
quests.question: Mutter
quests.hint: Think about saying something softly under your breath so almost no one hears.
quests.explanation: Mutter means to speak quietly and unclearly, almost to yourself. We sometimes mutter when we are thinking!
quests.funFact: Muttering to yourself while solving a problem can actually help you think it through!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for speaking in an unclear, quiet way that is hard to understand?
quests.question: Mumble
quests.hint: Think about talking with your mouth barely moving, so words come out unclear.
quests.explanation: Mumble means to speak unclearly and quietly. It helps to speak up clearly instead of mumbling!
quests.funFact: Speaking slowly and clearly helps people understand you better than mumbling does!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for saying something suddenly and loudly because you feel excited?
quests.question: Exclaim
quests.hint: Think about shouting Wow the moment you see something amazing.
quests.explanation: Exclaim means to say something suddenly and loudly with excitement. We exclaim Wow when we see something amazing!
quests.funFact: The punctuation mark that shows excitement is called an exclamation point!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for telling a group of people some important news?
quests.question: Announce
quests.hint: Think about a teacher telling the whole class some exciting news.
quests.explanation: Announce means to tell a group some important news. Our teacher announces a fun field trip!
quests.funFact: Announcing good news is even more fun when everyone gets to hear it together!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for talking with someone in a friendly, relaxed way?
quests.question: Chat
quests.hint: Think about talking easily with a friend about your day.
quests.explanation: Chat means to talk with someone in a friendly way. We chat with our friends at lunchtime!
quests.funFact: A friendly chat with someone is a wonderful way to build a strong friendship!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for sharing your thoughts about something out loud?
quests.question: Comment
quests.hint: Think about sharing your opinion about a story your class just read.
quests.explanation: Comment means to share your thoughts about something. We comment on a story we just read!
quests.funFact: Sharing a thoughtful comment can help start an interesting conversation!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for saying something out loud from memory?
quests.question: Recite
quests.hint: Think about saying a poem out loud that you learned by heart.
quests.explanation: Recite means to say something out loud from memory. We recite a poem we memorized at school!
quests.funFact: Reciting something many times helps you remember every single word!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for asking someone questions to learn about them?
quests.question: Interview
quests.hint: Think about asking your grandparent questions about when they were young.
quests.explanation: Interview means to ask someone questions to learn about them. We interview our grandparents about the past!
quests.funFact: Reporters interview people to learn interesting facts for the news!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for showing a skill, like singing or acting, in front of others?
quests.question: Perform
quests.hint: Think about standing on a stage to sing or act in front of an audience.
quests.explanation: Perform means to show a skill in front of others. We perform a song in the school show!
quests.funFact: Performers often practice for many weeks before they perform on stage!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for pretending to be someone else in a play or show?
quests.question: Act
quests.hint: Think about pretending to be a brave knight in a school play.
quests.explanation: Act means to pretend to be someone else in a play. We act out our favorite story characters!
quests.funFact: Actors practice their lines again and again before they act in a show!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for practicing a performance before doing it for real?
quests.question: Rehearse
quests.hint: Think about practicing your lines for a play many times before the real show.
quests.explanation: Rehearse means to practice a performance beforehand. We rehearse our school play before opening night!
quests.funFact: Rehearsing again and again helps every performer feel calm and confident!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for creating a brand new piece of music or writing?
quests.question: Compose
quests.hint: Think about making up your very own tune on a piano.
quests.explanation: Compose means to create a new piece of music or writing. We compose our own simple songs!
quests.funFact: Famous composers wrote beautiful music that people still enjoy today!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for telling a story out loud as it happens?
quests.question: Narrate
quests.hint: Think about telling a story out loud while everyone looks at the pictures.
quests.explanation: Narrate means to tell a story out loud. We narrate a story while showing the picture book!
quests.funFact: A narrator's voice can make a story feel even more exciting to listen to!
